lesson.title: Our Greeting Circle: A Week of Words with Sol
lesson.subject: spanish

contentBlocks.text: Today is our biggest day yet — a greeting circle with Sol! Let's use every word you learned this week.
Stand in your circle. Wave to Sol and say hola! Then say gracias when Sol hands you something, and por favor when you want more.
Sol asks you silly yes-or-no questions — answer sí or no! Then it's morning time: say buenos días and stretch. Now it's night time: say buenas noches and curl up.
You said hola, adiós, buenos días, buenas noches, gracias, por favor, sí, and no — all eight words! Wave goodbye to Sol and say adiós — see you next week to meet new friends!

objectives: Recall and use all eight of this week's greeting and courtesy words in one continuous greeting-circle routine
Initiate a greeting exchange with hola and close it with adiós
materialsNeeded: Family members or stuffed animals to complete a 'circle' (works fine with just you and your child too)
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Gather everyone available (family members, stuffed animals, or just the two of you) into a circle with Sol.
2. Go around the circle: each person waves and says '¡Hola!' as their turn comes, echoing back if needed.
3. Practice courtesy: Sol 'hands out' a small treat or toy, and each person says '¡Por favor!' to ask and '¡Gracias!' to thank.
4. Ask 2-3 silly sí/no questions like Day 4's game, mixing in this week's other words.
5. Do one buenos días stretch and one buenas noches curl-up together as a group.
6. Close the circle: everyone waves and says '¡Adiós!' to Sol and to each other.
7. Complete the speed-review activity together, celebrating every correct match with a cheer.
differentiationTips: Struggling: skip the full circle format and just review the 8 words one-on-one with Sol at your own pace — the goal is confident recall, not a big production
Ready for more: let your child be 'Sol' for the whole circle, leading each greeting themselves
This is a celebration lesson — the goal is joyful, confident use of words your child already practiced, not teaching anything brand new
teacherGuide.answerKey: This is a cumulative spoken review — success looks like your child using most or all of hola, adiós, buenos días, buenas noches, gracias, por favor, sí, and no somewhere in the circle, with prompting as needed.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Closes the week's WA-WL-2015.1.1 Interpersonal Communication arc by having the child initiate and close a real (if simple) social exchange using every word taught this week — the scope-and-sequence's own Day 5 design for this band, giving the child one continuous, celebratory use of the material rather than an isolated drill.
